# All settings

<!-- Generated by tools/manual/gen_reference.py from config.py and the import page: do not edit. -->

This page lists every setting as it is written in a settings file or in `project.toml` (`[section]`, then `name = value`). For each setting it gives the default and, if the setting appears on the [import page](../guide/import-page.md), its label there. A channel can be given by its number or by its name.

## `[input]`

The input: the IDEAS export or the stack, the dataset, its channels and its pixel size.

| Setting | Default | On the import page | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `image` | (none) |  | The input file: an IDEAS export (.zip, with one folder per dataset) or an ImageJ hyperstack made by ImageStreamCombiner (.tif, with one frame per event). |
| `output` | `'output'` |  | The results are written to a folder inside this folder, named after the dataset (or the stack). |
| `max_events` | (empty) | Only the first N events (empty = all) | Analyze only the first N events (in order of object number). Empty means all events. |
| `dataset` | (empty) |  | IDEAS zip only: the dataset to analyze (a folder in the zip). Empty means the only dataset in the zip. |
| `channels` | `[]` |  | IDEAS zip only: the channels to load, as IDEAS channel numbers (Ch&lt;N&gt;). Channels that have a role are always loaded. |
| `channel_names` | `[]` |  | IDEAS zip only: the names of these channels, in the same order as in channels. |
| `pixel_size` | (empty) |  | The pixel size in µm per pixel. It is required for an IDEAS zip, because the files in the zip do not record it. |

## `[channels]`

The role of each channel, given by channel number or by channel name.

| Setting | Default | On the import page | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `brightfield` | `1` |  | The brightfield channel. |
| `marker_of_interest` | `2` |  | The marker whose enrichment at the interface is measured. Empty ("") means no marker of interest: the tool then determines only the cell types and their contacts. The membrane analysis needs a marker of interest. |
| `tumor` | `3` |  | The tumor-cell marker. |
| `immune` | `[4]` |  | The immune-cell marker or markers, as a list. With several markers, each is normalized and the results are summed (the phenotypic markers of macro 2.8). |
| `functional` | `[]` |  | The immune subtype markers, as a list. Each immune cell is called positive or negative for each of them (the functional markers of macro 2.8). |
| `marker_location` | `'nuclear'` | Tumor / immune markers | Where the tumor and immune markers stain: "nuclear" (the nucleus or the cytoplasm) or "membrane". This determines the image that Cellpose segments. |
| `cell_of_interest` | `'Immune cell'` | Marker of interest expressed in | The cell type that expresses the marker of interest: "Tumor cell" or "Immune cell". |

## `[segmentation]`

Cellpose, and the clean-up of the cells it finds.

| Setting | Default | On the import page | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `method` | `'cellpose'` |  | "cellpose" runs Cellpose. "labelmap" loads the labels from labelmap_file instead. |
| `labelmap_file` | (empty) |  | The labelmap_cells.tif (or the Fiji macro's .zip) of an earlier run. |
| `model` | `'cyto3'` | Model (cyto3, cpsam, or a path) | The Cellpose model: cyto3, cyto2, nuclei, and so on for Cellpose 3, or cpsam for Cellpose 4. It can also be the path of a model file. |
| `diameter` | `30.0` | Cell diameter (px) | The typical cell diameter in pixels. 0 means that Cellpose estimates it (Cellpose 3 only). |
| `flow_threshold` | `0.5` |  | The flow threshold of Cellpose. A higher value gives more cells, some of them less certain. |
| `cellprob_threshold` | `0.0` |  | The cell probability threshold of Cellpose. A lower value gives larger cells. |
| `use_gpu` | `true` | Use the GPU | Run Cellpose on the GPU. |
| `reuse_labels` | `true` | Reuse the previous Cellpose result if nothing changed | Reuse the Cellpose result of the previous run of the dataset if its input image and Cellpose settings have not changed (labelmap_cells.tif and its .json file in the dataset folder). When off, Cellpose always runs. |
| `montage_columns` | `0` | Montage columns (0 = square) | The number of events per row in the montage that Cellpose segments. 0 makes the montage about square. Setting it to the number of events gives a single row, as in the Fiji macro. |
| `cellpose_python` | (empty) | Python with Cellpose | The python.exe of an environment with Cellpose 3 or 4, or the folder of that environment (a venv, conda or pixi environment, or a project folder with .venv or .pixi). Empty means the environment of this program. |
| `erosion` | `1` | Shrink cells (px) | Shrink the cells by this many pixels at their border with the background. |
| `min_cell_size` | `100` | Min. cell size (px) | Cells smaller than this (in pixels, after shrinking) are removed. |
| `max_cell_size` | `10000` | Max. cell size (px) | Cells larger than this (in pixels, after shrinking) are removed. |
| `exclude_edge_cells` | `false` | Leave out cells cut by the image edge | Leave out cells that are cut by the edge of their event image. Such cells are always flagged in the column Edge, whether or not they are left out. |

## `[classification]`

The thresholds of the subtype markers, artefacts and pools.

| Setting | Default | On the import page | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `threshold_method` | `'Two populations'` | Threshold of the subtype markers | The method for the automatic threshold of the subtype markers, applied to log(intensity - min + 1). "Two populations" puts the threshold where a cell is as likely to belong to the positive population as to the negative one; when there is no second population, it uses the upper noise limit of the negative cells. "MaxEntropy" works as in macro 2.8. "MaxEntropy strict" raises the MaxEntropy threshold, if needed, to at least 2 robust SDs above the negative cells. "Otsu" is the fourth choice. A settings file also accepts "Yen" and "RenyiEntropy". |
| `thresholds` | `{}` | Thresholds set by hand (Apply in a dashboard) | Thresholds set by hand, by marker name, for example { "Subtype A" = 12.5 }, as background-subtracted intensities. They replace the automatic thresholds. |
| `artefact_min_positive` | (empty) | Artefact: positive in at least N subtype markers (0 = none) | A detection that is positive in at least this many subtype markers is an artefact, not a cell. Empty means all subtype markers (only with two or more of them). 0 means that no detection is an artefact. |
| `pool` | `'experiment'` | Classify together (one set of thresholds) | In a project, "experiment" classifies the datasets of each experiment together, with one set of thresholds. "dataset" classifies each dataset on its own. |

## `[membrane]`

The membrane profiles and the enrichment at the interface.

| Setting | Default | On the import page | Meaning |
|---|---|---|---|
| `analysis` | `false` | Membrane profiles and enrichment | Measure the membrane profiles and the enrichment at the interface. The interface table per event is always made, whether or not this is on. |
| `cells` | `[]` | Membrane of (e.g. Tumor, Immune, A+; empty = where the marker is expressed) | The cells whose membrane is measured, as a list. Each item is a cell type ("Tumor", "Immune"), an immune subtype as written in the tables ("Immune A+ B+"), or a marker ("A+" means the immune cells positive for A). Empty means the cell type set in channels.cell_of_interest. |
| `partners` | `[]` | Interface with (empty = the other cell type) | The partners whose contact forms the interface, written as for cells. Empty means the other cell type. |
| `thickness` | (empty) | Membrane / interface width (px) | In pixels: the width of the membrane band, which is also the distance at which cells count as touching. Empty means about 1.5 µm (2 px at 20x, 3 px at 40x, 5 px at 60x). |
| `straightening_width` | (empty) | Straightening width (px) | In pixels: the width of the band across the outline that is straightened. Empty means about 4.5 µm (5 px at 20x, 9 px at 40x, 13 px at 60x). This width lets the band reach the membrane where the outline lies a little outside it. |
| `max_histogram_value` | (empty) | Histogram maximum (SD) | The upper end of the histograms, in SD above the mean. The histograms start at -5. Empty means automatic: the 99th percentile of the interface values or of the control windows, whichever is higher (at least 5), rounded up to a whole number of bins. Values above the upper end are not counted. |
| `histogram_bin_width` | (empty) | Histogram bin width (SD) | The bin width of the histograms, in SD. Empty means automatic: the smallest of 0.1, 0.2, 0.25, 0.5, 1, 2.5, 5, 10, ... that gives at most 60 bins (usually 25 to 60). |
| `control_repeats` | `10` | Control windows per cell | The number of random control windows per cell without an interface. Each window is as long as the median interface. |
| `inside_only` | `false` | Straighten inside the measured cell only | Take the profile only from the part of the band that lies inside the measured cell. This is a sensitivity test, not a way to separate the two membranes: touching membranes are much closer together than the resolution, so every pixel at the interface contains signal from both. |
